We have applied template 1914393 to target, got two fragments: product side? The retrosynthetic direction: template is retro, so applying to target yields precursors. The result tuple: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So first fragment is a core aromatic with amide etc but missing the side chain? Actually original target had Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to triazine? Wait original: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. The fragment after break is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (the triazine with NH not substituted) and FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (the side chain with F and CCl). Good.

Now apply template 1914394 to the second fragment FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. Result: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So we get dichloromethane? Actually ClCCl is Cl-CH2-Cl? That's a reagent? The other fragment is FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (the same but aromatic phenyl without Cl). So we have broken the CCl substituent to ClCCl (CH2Cl?) and phenyl.

Now apply template 1914395 to the first fragment? Actually template 1914395 is about converting F-CH to O-CH? Wait retro template: O-CH -> F-CH. So applying to a fragment containing O-CH? Our first fragment is COc1... no F. Maybe we need to apply 1914395 to something else. The order required: 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395. So after 1914394 we have three fragments: fragment A: COc1... (call A), fragment B: FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (call B), fragment C: ClCCl (call C). Now we need to apply 1914395 to one of these fragments (likely B) to break the F? The template 1914395 transforms O-CH to F-CH in forward direction, so retro direction would convert F-CH to O-CH. So applying retro to B (which has F attached to carbon) would give O-CH fragment. Let's apply to B.
